newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian authorities censor stories, reporters say.
newsitem.headline: Serbian authorities censor stories, reporters say.

text.p: A group of journalists at Serbia's main state-run newspaper have accused their management of censoring coverage of opposition street demonstrations over the past week, independent media reported on Tuesday.
"We are concerned over the unprofessional coverage of current events on Serbia's political scene," said a letter signed by 45 reporters at Politika.

"We are not advocates of biased journalism but are in favour of respect of facts and events which are unfolding before the eyes of our readers," said the letter, quoted by the independent Beta news agency.
The newspaper, considered a mouthpiece of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic's government, has either ignored the peaceful protests or portrayed the opposition as terrorists.

The demonstrations, demanding the ruling Socialists recognise results of a local election, have drawn international attention, but Politika and other state-owned papers have buried the news on back pages.
The letter coincided with reports that authorities were clamping down on independent media.
An independent newspaper which has reported on the wave of protests said it was coming under pressure from a state-run printing press to cut its circulation from 230,000 to 80,000.

"The Borba printing works, which has been printing our paper for the past two months, has been pressurising us for several days already," Cvijetin Milivojevic, an editor at the Blic daily, told independent radio B-92.
President Slobodan Milosevic keeps a tight rein on the media and over the past year shut down an independent television station, a radio station in Smederevo, and a news weekly.
